newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends unchanged in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends unchanged in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed unchanged on Tuesday from its previous New York close after a markedly lacklustre trading day, gold dealers said.
Physical demand took a slight dip on Tuesday because of a small price hike but remained generally steady, traders noted.
"There was some shortcovering," said a gold trader at an international bullion firm.
Gold traders in Hong Kong were divided on market sentiment prior to the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting later on Tuesday, which sets U.S. interest rate policy.
"I'm not focused on that at all," said Anderson Cheung, chief bullion dealer at Swiss Bank Corp.
Cheung noted that the next International Monetary Fund (IMF) meeting on September 29 on gold sales would affect the market more than the FOMC meeting.
But some other dealers and traders noted that players were refraining from taking fresh positions, fearful of fallout from the FOMC meeting.

An increase in interest rates would likely be good for gold markets as stocks and bonds would suffer, one trader said. But he added that higher interest rates would increase the cost of carrying long gold positions.
"I think we've had a huge amount of pressure on the downside," said the chief bullion dealer at an international bank, noting he expected to see a bout of shortcovering.
Bullion ended at US$381.50/382.00 an ounce on Tuesday against New York's US$381.50/382.00 close on Monday.
Local gold ended HK$5 higher at HK$3,517 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its Monday fix at -6.
